title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy
sections: Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes the procedures for reimbursing expenses incurred by shore-based employees during business travel.
All travel-related expenses must be documented and submitted for approval in accordance with the procedures outlined in this section.
Employees are responsible for maintaining accurate records of all travel and expenses, including receipts, travel itineraries, and any other supporting documentation required for reimbursement.
Employees must ensure that all expenses are incurred in the performance of their job duties and are necessary for the completion of assigned tasks.
Reimbursements for travel and expenses are subject to the company's general expense policy and any additional guidelines provided by the relevant department.
The finance department will process reimbursement requests upon receipt of complete and properly documented submissions.
Approval and Booking

All business travel needs prior written approval from the line manager. The line manager must review and approve travel requests before any booking is made. Approval must be obtained through the company's internal approval system.

Once approved, travel bookings must be made through the company travel desk. The travel desk is responsible for arranging flights, accommodations, and transportation in accordance with company policy. Employees are not permitted to book travel directly without prior approval.

Employees must provide the travel desk with all necessary travel details, including itinerary, contact information, and emergency contact details. Failure to provide accurate information may result in delays or cancellation of the booking. The travel desk will not be held responsible for incomplete or incorrect information.

All travel-related expenses must be incurred in accordance with the approved booking. Employees are required to retain all receipts and documentation for audit purposes. The travel desk will not reimburse expenses that do not match the approved booking details.
Air Travel
All air travel must be booked through the company's approved travel agency to ensure compliance with corporate travel standards.
Employees are required to use economy class for flights with a duration of 8 hours or less, as determined by the flight schedule provided by the travel agency.
For flights exceeding 8 hours in duration, business class travel is permitted, subject to prior approval from the head of the travel department.
The travel agency will confirm the flight duration and class of service prior to booking, and this information will be recorded in the travel request log.
In the event of a flight delay or change, the travel department will reassess the class of travel based on the updated flight duration and notify the employee accordingly.
Accommodation

All employees are required to book and pay for accommodation through the company's approved travel booking system prior to departure. The system automatically applies the applicable hotel spending limit based on the destination city.
The hotel spending limit is USD 180 per night for all locations outside designated major cities. Employees must confirm the city classification before booking to ensure compliance.
In designated major cities, the hotel spending limit is USD 240 per night. These cities are defined in the company's travel guidelines and are updated annually.
Any discrepancies between the submitted expenses and the approved booking will result in the rejection of the claim and potential disciplinary action.
Meals and Daily Allowance
The daily meal allowance provided to employees while travelling is USD 60 per day, intended to cover standard food expenses during business trips.
Employees are required to submit itemized receipts for all meal expenses incurred, which must be dated and signed by the employee to confirm authenticity.
Alcohol is not reimbursed under this policy, regardless of the occasion or location of the meal.
The meal allowance is applicable for all business-related travel outside the employee’s regular place of residence, including international and domestic trips.
Reimbursement for meal expenses is subject to the company’s general expense policy and must align with the approved travel itinerary and purpose.
Travel on Public Holidays and Weekends
Employees who travel on a public holiday or weekend day in their home location will receive one day of time off in lieu for each such day, as defined in the Leave and Holiday Policy.
The one day of time off in lieu must be taken within 60 days of the travel date and is not deducted from annual leave.
The time off in lieu will be granted as a calendar day and must be scheduled in accordance with the Leave and Holiday Policy.
The Leave and Holiday Policy governs the allocation and use of time off in lieu, including any exceptions for overlapping leave periods.
Expense Claims

All expense claims must be submitted within 30 days of returning from the business trip. Claims submitted after this period will not be eligible for reimbursement unless exceptional circumstances are documented and approved by the Head of Finance.

Employees are required to provide original receipts or digital equivalents for all expenses, with a minimum value of USD 25, to support their claims. Receipts must include the date, location, and description of the expense.
Expense claims must be submitted through the company’s internal reimbursement portal within 14 days of the trip’s conclusion. Late submissions may result in delays or denial of reimbursement.
Reimbursements for approved claims will be issued via the company’s internal payment system. Employees must ensure their contact details are up to date in the system to receive payments promptly.
Items That Are Not Reimbursed

Traffic fines incurred by employees during business travel are not reimbursed. Employees are responsible for covering the cost of traffic fines incurred while operating company vehicles or during official travel.

Personal entertainment expenses, including but not limited to dining, recreational activities, and non-business-related events, are not reimbursed. Employees must ensure all expenses are directly related to official business activities.

Expenses related to personal entertainment, such as tickets to concerts, sporting events, or cultural performances, are not reimbursed. Employees are expected to use personal funds for such activities.

Employees are required to maintain accurate records of all expenses and must clearly distinguish between reimbursable and non-reimbursable costs. Personal entertainment and traffic fines must be clearly identified in expense reports.
Any expense classified as personal entertainment or a traffic fine must be excluded from reimbursement requests. Employees are responsible for ensuring such expenses are not submitted for approval.
The company reserves the right to audit expense reports and disallow reimbursement for any traffic fines or personal entertainment expenses identified during the review process.
Travel Advances
Travel advances are provided to employees for anticipated expenses incurred during business travel.
The advance amount is set at 80% of the estimated costs for the trip.
Employees must submit a detailed travel itinerary and expense forecast prior to departure to ensure accurate advance calculation.
Once approved, the advance is issued via a company-issued credit card or direct deposit to the employee’s personal account.
Employees are responsible for maintaining receipts and documentation for all expenses incurred during the trip.
Reimbursement is processed after the trip concludes, based on actual expenses not exceeding the approved advance amount.
